Degree LevelDegree LevelWe offer three levels of graduate education: Graduate Diplomas (typically less than one year); Master's degrees (one to two years), and Doctoral or PhD degrees (four years).
Master's
Doctoral
Diploma
Expected Duration (Years)Expected DurationThere are three, four-month terms per year starting September 1 (fall), January 1 (winter), and May 1 (summer). Most programs begin in the fall term, while others have different start dates. Students might take longer than the program duration to complete their degree.
Curriculum OptionsCurriculum OptionsWe offer three types of curriculum options: Course-based (which focuses primarily on learning through course-work), project-based and thesis-based, (both of which requires students to conduct major research in addition to their course work). Some degree programs offer more than one curriculum option to obtain the same degree.
Thesis-based
Course-based
Project-based
Academic LoadAcademic LoadSome programs offer flexibility in how students can complete their degree with both part-time and full-time options. Other programs require students to be registered full-time or part-time.
Some doctoral programs have a flex-time option. Students enrolled in flex-time studies pay full-time tuition fees for the first four years of their registration, and part-time fees until they complete their program.
Full-Time
Part-Time
Flex-Time
Degree Program TypeDegree Program TypeResearch Degree Programs focus on research, scholarship and creative activity, and prepare students for a wide variety of potential careers, including those directly related to academia.
Professional Degree Programs are intentionally designed to prepare students to apply their knowledge and evidence-based training and skills in professional/career settings. In some cases, they prepare students for specific professions.
Professional
Research
Optional Collaborative SpecializationsCollaborative SpecializationsA Collaborative Specialization is an intra-university graduate field of study that provides an additional multidisciplinary experience for students enrolled in and completing the degree requirements for one of a number of approved Master's and/or PhD programs. Students are able to obtain a degree in their home program, and an additional credential in one of 13 subject areas.
